source_policy.notes: Temporary private viewing/listening and limited research quotation are described by source; commercial reproduction, substantial extraction and unauthorized text/data mining are restricted. These are narrowly selected research references, not an audio/metadata dataset for redistribution. No audio downloaded or bundled. Do not ship recordings or this reference metadata as licensed assets. Obtain appropriate permission for reuse.

interpretation_policy: Documented observations are source-supported paraphrases. Roles, controls, oscillator colours, contours and all synthesis mechanisms are original untested hypotheses, not biological measurements or sample reconstructions. Exact species keys are supplied mapping IDs, not independently verified BirdWeather taxonomy API results.

shared_design_recommendation.principle: Separate immutable species character from context/phrase variant; related species can share a tonal core while preserving distinctive articulations. Do not infer character from taxonomy alone.
primitives: Bounded additive/harmonic tone with per-partial decay and spectral tilt.
Continuous pitch trajectory in semitones with optional bounded pitch/amplitude trill.
Fixed-capacity phrase cells with per-cell onset, duration, pitch, amplitude and timbre segment; compile off callback.
Optional deterministic band-limited noise and bounded roughness; independent tonal/noisy segment envelopes.
shared_design_recommendation.closest_family_pair: Bellbird and tui share Meliphagidae and a ringing song core, but tui rough interruptions provide a major contrast; population/context exceptions remain visible.
shared_design_recommendation.realtime_note: Research brief is not an implementation specification: state/update order, oscillator alias policy, sample-rate/reset behaviour, capacities and off-thread publication/retirement still need definition before production integration.

design_hypothesis.status: Designed from documented descriptions and varied recording contexts; not audition-validated or owner-approved.
design_hypothesis.musical_role: Low-register, rounded answering voice; paired pulses with a gently inflected second pulse, separated by generous silence.
design_hypothesis.desired_timbre_and_mechanism: Fundamental-dominant additive tone, weak upper harmonics, soft onset; optional brief upward whistle variant and slightly grainy repeated pulse. A paired phrase is essential to its identity.
design_hypothesis.control_value_provenance: Original provisional musical choice; tuning is relative to mapped note, not measured animal pitch. Gain is a starting compensation, not equal-loudness evidence.
design_hypothesis.distinct_identifying_gesture: Low-register, rounded answering voice; paired pulses with a gently inflected second pulse, separated by generous silence.
design_hypothesis.contrast_listening_test: Pair versus single-note ablation; distinguish from cuckoo rising whistle and from dry kingfisher repetitions.
gaps: No reference audio audition or spectrogram/pitch extraction.
No measured source Hz, timing, spectrum, noise ratio or loudness matching.
Four current controls cannot express the proposed species identity on their own.

design_hypothesis.musical_role: Pure whistled rising ostinato; each note bends upward, then a lower falling whistle closes the phrase.
design_hypothesis.desired_timbre_and_mechanism: Near-sine voice with light second harmonic; deterministic continuous upward curve within repeated notes and a terminal downward curve. Avoid a metallic bell tail or generic random chirps.
design_hypothesis.control_value_provenance: Original provisional musical choice; tuning is relative to mapped note, not measured animal pitch. Gain is a starting compensation, not equal-loudness evidence.
design_hypothesis.distinct_identifying_gesture: Pure whistled rising ostinato; each note bends upward, then a lower falling whistle closes the phrase.
design_hypothesis.contrast_listening_test: Compare with morepork rising alternative and tomtit downscale; cuckoo identity should come from repeated upsweeps and terminal falling gesture, not pitch alone.
